found_values.value: One output of the I/O expander per biased line, 5 in all: one for each of the 4 multiprotocol ports and one for the UART socket. A resistor holds each control input at the pull-down selection, so the reset and unpowered state selects the pull-down, which is the condition of V57's answer. The expander resets with the RP2354B and its driving pin is then an input (IOBoard.md:340). A jumper cannot follow a mode that firmware sets per binding (IOBoard.md:64). A circuit that follows the signal cannot tell the modes apart: bidirectional DShot and the UART-based modes idle high, and servo PWM and plain DShot idle low (IOBoard.md:251, :253, :256). An RP2354B GPIO also meets V57, because the pads reset pulled low (RP2350 section 9.3), but it costs 5 GPIO. How many outputs the expander has is V119 (R6, for research)

found_values.value: With the pin released, the UART socket and a multiprotocol port in ESC bootloader, ESC telemetry, servo configuration or VESC mode take a switched 1 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V. It sits in parallel with the fixed 10 kΩ pull-down, which puts the idle at 3.0 V. With the gate disabled, the line has the 10 kΩ pull-down alone while the selector is at its reset or unpowered state (V57). A disabled line whose pull-up firmware keeps selected idles at 3.0 V. Evidence: AM32's bootloader samples the line against its own pull-down and stays only when the line reads high and never low (bootloader/main.c:1097-1138); it then receives with its pull-up (main.c:516). BLHeli_S's bootloader sets its pin open-drain and high ('Disable pushpull', 'Set data high') and waits while the line is high, so its high level comes from a pull-up. AM32's G071 KISS telemetry pin is open-drain with the MCU pull-up (serial_telemetry.c:27-28). A Hitec D-series servo drives low only and holds a 3 kΩ pull-down, and the library asks for a 1 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V on a 3.3 V controller (HitecDServoInternal.h, Fundamentals; README.md:11). OpenYGE is UART 8N1 (docs/OpenYGE.md:21) and idles high. Why 1 kΩ: against the servo's 3 kΩ and the board's 10 kΩ (2.31 kΩ together), the line sits at 3.3 × 2.31 / 3.31 = 2.30 V, above the RP2350's 2.0 V V_IH (Table 1436). A pull-up above 1.50 kΩ puts it below 2.0 V

One signal wire, the servo's PWM signal line, at half duplex. UART with inverted polarity: idle low, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit. The servo's output drives low only, and the servo holds a 3 kΩ pull-down; the programmer supplies the pull-up. After power-up or a write to the REBOOT register, the servo ignores PWM and serial for 1000 ms and holds the line low. After a serial command it ignores PWM until it reboots. Source status as V60

3.3 V, driven from the 3.3 V rail, on the 16 PWM ports, the 4 multiprotocol ports and the UART socket. No supply is sensed from the device. Evidence: an ESCape32 ESC's own signal line reads about 3.3 V after a power cycle (Installation page). SRXL2 is standard 3.3 V logic. CRSF runs at 3.3 V at half duplex and at 3.0 to 3.3 V at full duplex. A Hitec D-series servo reads about 2 V as high. KISS telemetry is sent at 3.6 V. No source read requires 5 V. The input thresholds of servos other than Hitec D-series are not read. The connector side takes at least 3.6 V, with the board powered or unpowered

found_values.value: 1 kΩ to 3.3 V. It is the switched pull-up of V58, in parallel with the fixed 10 kΩ pull-down, and the idle sits at 3.0 V. The pull-up only holds the idle, because both ESC firmwares read drive the reply push-pull. AM32 drives it from a timer output (Mcu/g071/Src/IO.c, sendDshotDma). Bluejay sets its pin push-pull for the reply (src/Modules/Isrs.asm, 'Set output mode to push-pull'). AM32 targets pull their input up, except NEUTRONRC_G071, which pulls it down (Src/main.c:1930-1934). With the pull-up selected, the RP2354B sinks (3.3 − 0.5) V / 1 kΩ = 2.8 mA while it drives low. That is within the 4 mA drive setting at V_OL ≤ 0.5 V (Table 1436). One value serves every mode that idles high, because Hitec servo configuration needs 1.50 kΩ or less (V58)

Low, on every gated line, both while the RP2354B is held in reset and while it restarts through the watchdog. Held in reset by RUN or by a brownout, the pads return to their reset state: output at high impedance, input disabled, pulled low at 36 to 113 kΩ (section 9.3; Table 1436). The isolation latches reset with them (section 9.7). A 244's inputs then read low: its input leakage of ±5 µA through 113 kΩ gives 0.57 V, under V_IL 0.8 V, so it drives low. The switch passes the pad's low, and the 10 kΩ pull-down holds the line. The expander resets with the RP2354B, and the control resistors select the pull-down. Through a watchdog reset, the pads return to the same state when the watchdog's reset level includes RESETS. pico-sdk's _watchdog_enable sets PSM_WDSEL for every stage except ROSC and XOSC (section 12.9.6.1, lines 52-53). Bit 4 of PSM WDSEL is RESETS (Table 532). The RESETS reset value holds PADS_BANK0 (bit 9) and IO_BANK0 (bit 6) in reset (Table 535). A PADS reset returns each pad whose ISO bit software has cleared to its reset state (section 9.7), and gpio_set_function() clears ISO (section 9.3). If firmware leaves RESETS out of PSM_WDSEL, and PADS_BANK0 and IO_BANK0 out of RESETS_WDSEL, the pads keep their pre-reset level. The tree enables no watchdog yet (IOBoard.md:221). Not established: whether a watchdog reset with POWMAN_WDSEL.RESET_SWCORE set (Table 490, reset value 0, not set by the SDK) asserts the isolation signal and latches the pre-reset pad state

found_values.value: Yes, on the 4 multiprotocol ports, the UART socket and the receiver input. Devices on their own supply drive these lines while the IO board is unpowered: a receiver on its own pack; SRXL2 devices on servo-bus power of 3.5 to 8.4 V (SRXL2 spec section 5); an ESC on the operator's pack during programming (V78). The RP2354B's fault-tolerant pins take 3.63 V with IOVDD at 0 V, and 'very little current' flows, with no figure given (Tables 1426 and 1433). The powered-off isolation rule covers every interlock input driven while its own supply is absent (Monostable.md:65-88)

found_values.value: Both faults, continuous: a short to ground, and a short to the port's supply pin at up to 8.7 V (F16). The lead carries signal, ground and rail in one plug (IOBoard.md:531), and nothing in the tree limits the current into a shorted signal line (IOBoard.md:536). Derived series resistance per gated line, placed between the gate element and the connector, with the clamp and the bias network (switched 1 kΩ pull-up, 10 kΩ pull-down) on the gate element's side. Lower bound: a line driven by the RP2354B pad through the switch takes at least 275 Ω (3.3 V / 12 mA, the highest drive setting Table 1436 characterises); a line driven by a 244 takes at least 142 Ω (3.4 V at its 24 mA recommended output current). Upper bound on the multiprotocol and UART lines in servo configuration mode: the servo's open-drain low reaches the RP2354B pin through the resistor, against the 1 kΩ pull-up. At 275 Ω it stays at or below V_IL 0.8 V (Table 1436) only while the servo's output-low voltage is 0.13 V or less; with the servo at 0 V it is 0.70 V. At 300 Ω the servo's output-low voltage must be 0.05 V or less. No source read states the servo's output-low voltage, so no value is shown to meet both bounds. With the bias network on the connector side instead, the bench's low reaches the connector at 1.02 V through 275 Ω with the pad at its guaranteed V_OL of 0.5 V, and the servo's input-low threshold is not stated. A short to 8.7 V puts (8.7 − 3.6) / 275 = 18.5 mA into a 3.6 V clamp and 95 mW into the resistor. The resistor and the clamp are round 2 parts (Research.md, Scope)
found_values.source: IOBoard.md:531, :536; F16 (Research.md:544); RP2350 datasheet build-date 2025-07-29 Table 1436; SN74LVC244A SCAS414AG section 5.3 (IOH −24 mA at 3 V); SN74CBTLV3126 SCDS038N section 5.5 (ron); HitecDServoInternal.h (3 kΩ pull-down); nodal derivation in this return

A STOP, then the operator clear of the F11 latch; no separate switch. The ESC pack switch and the buffer enable both follow the enable node alone (R3 row, Research.md:281). The pack switch closes within 500 ms of the enable rising (V46 answer, Research.md:606), and the gate enables at once. With the programming mode bound before the clear, the RP2354B holds the line high with the pull-up selected, so the ESC powers up with its line high. What the bootloaders need: AM32 stays in its bootloader only when the line reads high and never low at start-up (bootloader/main.c:1097-1138). BLHeli_S waits while the line is high and leaves after about 250 ms (BLHeliBootLoad.inc, BOOT_DELAY). ESCape32 needs the line high for 2 s at start-up. A Hitec D-series servo needs no power cycle: firmware reboots it through its REBOOT register, and it accepts serial 1000 ms later. VESC's UART needs none. Whether the latch sets on the level or on the edge (V52, R3) does not change this

No Hitec publication of the D-series protocol was found. The only source is the reverse-engineered HitecDServo library, which states it is not endorsed by Hitec: 115,200 baud, inverted, half duplex, a servo that drives low only with a 3 kΩ pull-down. docs/Manifest.md:32 calls the protocol published

The multiprotocol and UART lines are driven by the RP2354B pads through SN74CBTLV3126 and the series resistor: V_OH ≥ 2.62 V and V_OL ≤ 0.5 V at the 2, 4, 8 or 12 mA setting. The 1 kΩ pull-up needs a 4 mA setting or higher (2.8 mA sunk). The sum of all GPIO source current is 100 mA at most
